title: Tensor Koszul coordinates for adjoining the final generator
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, M an R-module, r a natural number and f : Fin (r+1) -> R. Put g(i)=f(i.castSucc), A=K(g) tensor_R M and B=K(f) tensor_R M, with the complexes of [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex]. There exist R-linear equivalences e0 : B_0 -> A_0 and e_n : B_(n+1) -> A_(n+1) direct_sum A_n for every n>=0. They satisfy e0(d_B x)=d_A(e_0 x).first + f(last r)*(e_0 x).second for x in B_1, and e_n(d_B x)=(d_A(e_(n+1) x).first + f(last r)*(e_(n+1) x).second, -d_A(e_(n+1) x).second) for x in B_(n+2). There is no regularity or nonzero-module hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 0628 and 0629, cone of multiplication by the final generator; step 2 of the regular-sequence node; read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/062F and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0629 because the literature source is not present on this machine

proof.text: Use the explicit assembly bijection [lem-weil-pbc-koszul-last-generator-assembly] in every positive exterior degree. Degree zero uses exteriorPower.zeroEquiv and its naturality from [lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis]. Turn the assembly maps into linear equivalences with LinearEquiv.ofBijective; their inverses are determined uniquely by the explicit maps. Tensor their inverses with M and compose with TensorProduct.prodLeft.

Prove contraction commutes with the prefix exterior-algebra map by left induction and linearCombination_comp_lmapDomain. Apply contractLeft_ι_mul to the second assembly summand: its contraction is f(last r) times the included b minus the last generator times the included prefix contraction. This proves the higher-degree formula on untensored assembly elements. In degree zero, every prefix scalar is an algebraMap element and has zero contraction, giving the separate degree-one formula.

Use tensor-product induction. For each pure tensor choose its unique exterior assembly coordinates using the bijection, apply the proved untensored boundary formula, and use rTensor_tmul, prodLeft_tmul, add_tmul, smul_tmul and neg_tmul. The zero and sum cases follow by linearity and additive rearrangement. ChainComplex.of_d identifies the displayed complex differentials with the tensor boundaries. This yields both formulas with arbitrary M, including r=0.

lean.statement: theorem exists_koszulTensorConeCoordinates {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (M : Type v) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {r : ℕ} (f : Fin (r + 1) → R) : let A := koszulComplexTensor R r (fun i ↦ f i.castSucc) M let B := koszulComplexTensor R (r + 1) f M ∃ (e₀ : B.X 0 ≃ₗ[R] A.X 0) (e : ∀ n : ℕ, B.X (n + 1) ≃ₗ[R] A.X (n + 1) × A.X n), (∀ x : B.X 1, e₀ (B.d 1 0 x) = A.d 1 0 (e 0 x).1 + f (Fin.last r) • (e 0 x).2) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (x : B.X (n + 2)), e n (B.d (n + 2) (n + 1) x) = (A.d (n + 2) (n + 1) (e (n + 1) x).1 + f (Fin.last r) • (e (n + 1) x).2, -A.d (n + 1) n (e (n + 1) x).2))
